senses.gloss:
Oṅkāreśvara
------------------------------------------
Places of पिल्ग्रिमगे are a source of inspiration and symbols of cultural unity.
Among the well-known places of पिल्ग्रिमगे associated with lord शिव, those containing the ज्योतिर्लिङ्गस् (literally, ‘liṅgas of light’, twelve in number, spread all over India) are considered extremely sacred. The ओङ्कारेश्वर (the लिङ्ग and the temple containing it) is classed among these twelve.
Oṅkāreśvara TempleThe ओङ्कारेश्वर temple is situated on the Māndhātā island inside the नर्मदा river, the two streams that surround it being known as नर्मदा and कावेरी (not the कावेरी of South India). Inside it there are actually two Śivaliṅgas —Oṅkāreśvara and Amaleśvara—both considered as ‘Jyotirliṅgas’ but calculated as one only. The emperor Māndhātā of the इक्ष्वाकु race (same as the रघु-race) is said to have realised Lord शिव here.
The area of this island is about 2.6 sq. kms. (1 sq. mile). The shape of the island resembles that of ॐ (Om). Hence the name ‘Oṅkāreśvara’.
It is said that the god विन्ध्य (the supervising deity of the विन्ध्य mountains) once propitiated Lord शिव here through a यन्त्र (sacred geometrical diagram) and a लिङ्ग of sand (or clay). Pleased with his worship, शिव appeared before him and agreed to stay on in those two forms. These two forms—the यन्त्र and the earthen image—later on became the two liṅgas which we now see. The Oṅkāreśvaraliṅga is a natural one (svayambhū or udbhava लिङ्ग) and is surrounded by water. Entrance to the temple is small. Images of पार्वती and fivefaced गणपति are also established inside the temple.
The temple can be approached by boat.
There are quite a few temples around the ओङ्कारेश्वर shrine, on the island.
See also NARMADĀ.
